semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1, for all real numbers t with (n minus 1) divided by n <= t and t < 1, and for all integers k with 1 <= k <= n, the floor of k times t equals k minus 1.

variables.role: parameter controlling the value inside the floor via multiplication with k

variables.name: k
variables.role: inner quantified parameter; argument of floor is k*t and RHS is k-1

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k-1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

From t < 1 we get k t < k.
From t >= (n-1)/n we get
k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 <= k t < k.

Because k-1 is an integer and it is the greatest integer not exceeding k t, it follows that floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary, this holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.
result_payload.proof_summary: For k in {1,...,n}, the bounds (n-1)/n <= t < 1 imply k-1 <= kt < k, so the floor is exactly k-1.
